extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic/anabelian geometry (readers of Mochizuki's IUT / specialists in tempered and pro-Σ fundamental groups)
extracted.subtask_description: Group-theoretic characterizations and reconstruction criteria for fundamental groups, decomposition/inertia groups, and edge/vertex subgroups of (pro-)Σ / tempered fundamental groups associated to hyperbolic curves and semi-graphs of anabelioids; includes criteria for ramification, cuspidal/nodal/verticial subgroup identification, and commensurable terminality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic Nature of Coverings / reconstructability
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose k is an NF or an MLF. There exists a functorial group-theoretic algorithm to reconstruct Π_X, Π_{C→}, Π_C (respectively Π_C) together with the conjugacy classes of the decomposition groups determined by specified sets of cusps from Π_{X→} (respectively Π_{C→}). The reconstruction is functorial with respect to isomorphisms of topological groups and recovers these groups as subgroups of Aut(Π_{X→}) (respectively Aut(Π_{C→})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm recovers l via the formula l^2 = [Δ_X : Δ_X] · [Δ_X : Δ_{X→}] = [Δ_X : Δ_{X→}] = [Δ_C : Δ_{X→}]/2 (as written in the paper) and uses slimness and embedding results (Π_{X→}, Π_X, Π_C slim) and group-theoretic identification of decomposition groups (images nontrivial in Gal(X→/X)). Works similarly in resp'd and non-resp'd cases; see references AbsTopI/II, AbsTopIII for algorithmic meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoreticity of total ramification for (pro-)l cyclic coverings
rubrics_metrics.description: Given finite étale coverings Z_i → V_i → X_i with Z_i cyclic of degree a power of l over V_i, one may determine group-theoretically whether Z_i → V_i is totally ramified (i.e., at some point of Z_i). This condition is equivalent to existence of a factorization Z_i → W_i → V_i where W_i → V_i is finite étale of degree l and r_{W_i} < l · r_{V_i}. The characterization extends to pro-l cyclic coverings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, inertia groups of cusps in (Δ_{X_i})(l) (the maximal pro-l quotient of Δ_{X_i}) may be characterized group-theoretically as the maximal subgroups of (Δ_{X_i})(l) corresponding to (pro-)l coverings satisfying this total-ramification condition. See amended text replacing part of AbsAnab Lemma 1.3.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of decomposition groups of cusps via Z_l-subgroups and chi-inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition groups of cusps ⊆ H* may be characterized group-theoretically as the maximal closed subgroups I ⊆ H* isomorphic to Z_l which satisfy: for every characteristic open subgroup J ⊆ H* with J ≠ I·J, the inequality dχ_cyclo_G(((I·l·J)^{ab} ⊗ Q_l)) + 1 < l · {dχ_cyclo_G(((I·J)^{ab} ⊗ Q_l)) + 1} holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the final portion of AbsTopI Lemma 4.5(iv). The inequality is interpreted as the group-theoretic condition that the covering of curves corresponding to J ⊆ I·J is totally ramified at some cusp. Use this to single out decomposition groups among Z_l-subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cuspidally totally ramified criterion for cyclic coverings (r-inequality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G' → G be a Galois finite étale covering of degree a positive power of l with G' cyclic. Then G' → G is cuspidally totally ramified iff the inequality r(G') < l · r(G) is satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Π_unr_G-coverings (with n(G') = deg(G'/G) · n(G)), G' → G is verticially purely totally ramified iff i(G') = deg(G'/G) · (i(G) − 1) + 1; equivalently i(G') − n(G') = deg(G'/G) · (i(G) − n(G) − 1) + 1. These formulas give group-theoretic numerical tests for (cuspidal/verticial) total ramification; see replacement for CombGC Remark 1.4.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verticially purely totally ramified criterion (i-formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering is verticially purely totally ramified iff i(G') = deg(G'/G) · (i(G) − 1) + 1. Equivalently, i(G') − n(G') = deg(G'/G) · (i(G) − n(G) − 1) + 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an exact arithmetic/graph-theoretic equality to detect verticial pure total ramification in the pro-Σ / Π_unr context; useful when analyzing coverings that are Π_unr_G-coverings or when counting invariants i(·), n(·).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cuspidal edge-like subgroup characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Cuspidal edge-like subgroups of ΠG are the maximal closed subgroups A ⊆ ΠG isomorphic to Z_l which satisfy: for every characteristic open subgroup ΠG(2) ⊆ ΠG, writing G' → G'' → G for the finite étale coverings corresponding to A · ΠG(2) ⊆ ΠG, the cyclic finite étale covering G' → G'' is cuspidally totally ramified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessity is immediate from definitions; sufficiency follows since the finiteness of cusps in finite étale coverings implies existence of a compatible system of cusps stabilized by A. This characterization identifies cuspidal edge-like Z_l-subgroups purely group-theoretically; see replacement of CombGC Remark 1.4.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unramified verticial subgroup / vertex characterization via M_unr quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sturdy G, let M^{unr}_G[v] be images of Π^{unr}_G-conjugacy classes of unramified verticial subgroups associated to vertex v. Consider elementary abelian quotients φ: M^{unr}_G → Q (identify by kernel, order by domination). Such a quotient corresponds to a verticially purely totally ramified covering iff there exists a vertex v with φ(M^{unr}_G[v]) = Q. The set of vertices of G is characterized as the set of nontrivial quotients M^{unr}	ext{-}vert_G[v] ⊗ F_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One identifies maximal quotients among these elementary abelian quotients (relative to domination) and their restriction properties; the characterization allows recovery of vertices (and hence unramified verticial subgroups) functorially from group-theoretic quotients. See detailed replacement text in CombGC Remark 1.4.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nodal edge-like subgroup characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: If G is pro-Σ PSC-type and noncuspidal, the nodal edge-like subgroups of ΠG are the maximal closed subgroups A ⊆ ΠG isomorphic to Z_l such that for every characteristic open subgroup ΠG(2) ⊆ ΠG, writing G' → G'' → G for coverings corresponding to A · ΠG(2), the cyclic finite étale covering G' → G'' is nodally totally ramified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moreover, a finite étale covering G' → G'' is nodally totally ramified iff it is module-wise nodal. This yields a group-theoretic test to select nodal edge-like Z_l-subgroups; see replacement of CombGC Remark 1.4.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profinite conjugates of nontrivial compact subgroups imply tempered membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Λ ⊆ Π^{tp}_G be a nontrivial compact subgroup and γ ∈ (cid:10)Π_G an element such that γ · Λ · γ^{-1} ⊆ Π^{tp}_G (equivalently Λ ⊆ γ^{-1} · Π^{tp}_G · γ). Then γ ∈ Π^{tp}_G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 2.1: the proof reduces to verticial subgroup arguments and tempered/pro-(cid:10)Γ vertex considerations (use Γ^{tp} → (cid:10)Γ density and temperedness of vertices). This gives a rigidity criterion: conjugating a nontrivial compact into Π^{tp}_G forces the conjugator to lie in Π^{tp}_G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commensurable terminality of subgroups associated to sub-semi-graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: (cid:10)Π_H (respectively Π^{tp}_H) is commensurably terminal in (cid:10)Π_G (respectively in (cid:10)Π_G and hence in Π^{tp}_G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 2.2: This follows from Proposition 2.1 by allowing Λ to range over open subgroups of verticial subgroups; yields centrality/terminality statements for subgroups coming from stabilized sub-semi-graphs H ⊆ G. Use pro-(cid:10)Σ completion arguments and commensurable terminality definitions (C(·)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commensurable terminality and outer-action determination for tempered subgroups (Corollary 2.3(i,ii,iv,v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a stable reduction set-up with H a G_k-stable sub-semi-graph: (i) the closed subgroups Δ^{tp}_{X,H} := Δ^{tp}_X ×_{Π^{tp}_G} Π^{tp}_H ⊆ Δ^{tp}_X and (cid:10)Δ_{X,H} := (cid:10)Δ_X ×_{(cid:10)Π_G} (cid:10)Π_H ⊆ (cid:10)Δ_X are commensurably terminal; the natural outer actions of G_k on Δ^{tp}_X determine outer actions on Δ^{tp}_{X,H}, (cid:10)Δ_{X,H}. (ii) The closure of Δ^{tp}_{X,H} in (cid:10)Δ_X equals (cid:10)Δ_{X,H}. (iv) Images of natural inclusions Π^{tp}_{X,H} → Π^{tp}_X and (cid:10)Π_{X,H} → (cid:10)Π_X are commensurably terminal. (v) Δ^{tp}_X = Δ^{tp}_{X,H} ⊆ (cid:10)Δ_X (equality statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assertions use the previous propositions and density/closure arguments for pro-(cid:10)Σ completions together with tempered/pro-(cid:10)Σ group relations. They provide group-theoretic control of subgroups attached to sub-semi-graphs and how arithmetic G_k-outer actions restrict. See Corollary 2.3 for precise hypotheses and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slimness and exact sequences for tempered subgroups (Corollary 2.3(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If either (a) (cid:10)Σ contains the residue characteristic p or (b) (cid:10)Σ = Primes, then (cid:10)Δ_{X,H} is slim. In particular, for a prime l ∉ Σ the natural outer actions of G_k on Δ^{tp}_{X,H}, (cid:10)Δ_{X,H} determine natural exact sequences of center-free topological groups: 1 → Δ^{tp}_{X,H} → Π^{tp}_{X,H} → G_k → 1 and 1 → (cid:10)Δ_{X,H} → (cid:10)Π_{X,H} → G_k → 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two proofs are indicated: an elementary one requiring (a) and one using Tamagawa's results requiring (b). Uses density and pro-Σ arguments plus construction of suitable open subgroups J to force nonabelian pro-Σ completions on components, then deduce triviality of centralizers. These give exact, center-free group extensions in the tempered/pro-(cid:10)Σ setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inertia group localization equivalence (Corollary 2.3(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Let I_x be an inertia group in Δ^{tp}_X (resp (cid:10)Δ_X) associated to a cusp x of X, and ξ the cusp of the stable model corresponding to x. Then the following are equivalent: (a) I_x lies in a Δ^{tp}_X- (resp (cid:10)Δ_X-) conjugate of Δ^{tp}_{X,H} (resp (cid:10)Δ_{X,H}); (b) ξ meets an irreducible component of the special fiber of X that is contained in H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a geometric ↔ group-theoretic equivalence locating inertia groups via containment/conjugacy in the tempered/pro-(cid:10)Σ subgroup attached to H. Useful for identifying which cusps/inertia groups correspond to components inside H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic analogue: profinite conjugates imply tempered membership and terminality (Proposition 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) If Λ ⊆ Δ^{tp}_X is a nontrivial pro-Σ compact subgroup and γ ∈ (cid:10)Π_X satisfies γ · Λ · γ^{-1} ⊆ Δ^{tp}_X (equivalently Λ ⊆ γ^{-1} · Δ^{tp}_X · γ), then γ ∈ Π^{tp}_X. (ii) If (cid:10)Σ = Primes and Λ ⊆ Π^{tp}_X is a nontrivial compact subgroup whose image in G_k is open, then any γ ∈ (cid:10)Π_X with γ · Λ · γ^{-1} ⊆ Π^{tp}_X lies in Π^{tp}_X. (iii) Δ^{tp}_X (resp Π^{tp}_X) is commensurably terminal in (cid:10)Δ_X (resp (cid:10)Π_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arithmetic variant of Proposition 2.1 and 2.2; proofs use reduction to pro-Σ semi-graph G_J attached to finite-index characteristic J ⊆ Δ^{tp}_X, application of Proposition 2.1 on that semi-graph, and passage to inverse limits; (ii) uses arithmetic analogues from SemiAnbd Theorems and temperedness arguments. Part (iii) follows by allowing Λ to range over Sylow/open subgroups of decomposition groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Containment / uniqueness criterion for decomposition and inertia groups in tempered completions (Corollary 2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume (cid:10)Σ = Primes. Every decomposition group in (cid:10)Π_X (resp every inertia group in (cid:10)Π_X) associated to a closed point or cusp of X (resp to a cusp of X) is contained in Π^{tp}_X (resp the corresponding inertia group in Π^{tp}_X). Moreover, a (cid:10)Π_X-conjugate of Π^{tp}_X contains a decomposition group in Π^{tp}_X iff it equals Π^{tp}_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a uniqueness/rigidity statement: decomposition/inertia groups arising in the pro-(cid:10)Σ completion actually live in the tempered subgroup, and containment of a tempered decomposition group inside a conjugate characterizes equality. Use Proposition 2.4 and the arithmetic tempered arguments in the proof.
